item.text:
**Overall**
Mostly yes. Kishida’s 2024 record shows social-service funding and management through formal councils, expert panels, BOJ discipline, and rule-based budget guidelines. The main counterweight is that political-scandal pressure and coalition survival bargaining were still present, so technocratic management was real but not fully insulated from politics.

**Positive**
- **Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html)  
  Kishida tied 2024 to **wage growth, child support, disaster recovery, women’s participation, public education, dementia policy, and regional revitalization**, and said funding would come through expenditure reform. That is strong evidence of formal, programmatic social-service management rather than patronage.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`

- **Policies supporting children and child-rearing** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024 page content | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/ongoingtopics/policies_kishida/childsupport.html)  
  The cabinet page lays out a structured package: **child allowances, reduced childbirth and higher-education burdens, housing support for child-rearing households, prenatal/postnatal care, and stronger early-childhood education and childcare**. This is policy design through administrative systems, not clientelist handouts.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`

- **Meeting of the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-04-19 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202404/19keizai.html)  
  Kishida said regional revitalization required **sustainable local services, digital tools, and grants**, indicating social-service administration that tries to build capacity in poorer areas through ordinary public institutions.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `6B.3`, `6B.2`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-21 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202406/21kaiken.html)  
  Kishida backed expanded subsidies for **school lunches, agriculture, SMEs, medical and nursing care, childcare, school facilities, public transport, logistics, regional tourism, and low-income households**. The package was routed through formal policy channels and aimed at broad service delivery, not partisan distribution.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `5B.8`

- **Meeting of Experts to Review Active Cyber Defense** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-06-07 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202406/07cyber.html)  
  Although not a welfare policy, it shows the broader governing style: Kishida convened a **17-expert panel** to shape legislation, which is consistent with a technocratic approach to state capacity rather than patronage networks.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `5B.2`, `5B.6`

- **Policy Speech by Prime Minister Kishida to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-30 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html)  
  The same speech also says the government would pursue **reskilling, labor-market reform, infrastructure, capital investment, and cyber/legal preparation** through formal policy structures. That supports a reading of professionalized public management rather than personal-network control.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `5B.6`, `5B.7`

- **Prime Minister Kishida’s Statements after the Earthquake Response** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-01-25 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/25kaiken.html)  
  The disaster package used **cash aid, emergency housing, reduced medical/nursing-care burdens, and support for schools and transit**, which is targeted service delivery through the state rather than patronage.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `6B.2`, `6B.3`, `5B.9`

- **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-03-19 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/19kaiken.html)  
  Kishida accepted the BOJ’s judgment that a **price-wage virtuous cycle** had been confirmed and said the government would preserve the existing accord, which is evidence of rule-based macro management supporting public-service funding stability.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`

- **July 29 budget-guidelines decision** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | 2024-07-29 | [URL](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/actions/202407/29keizai.html)  
  Kishida approved budget guidelines based on **medium- to long-term projections** and framed policy around **private-demand-led growth and wage increases above inflation**. That is technocratic budget management, not patronage budgeting.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `5B.1`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`

**Mixed / Negative**
- **Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget** | Reuters | 2024-02-28 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362)  
  Reuters reported Kishida was pulled into defensive political management over the funding scandal, which suggests some budget and reform decisions were shaped by short-term survival pressure rather than purely professional administration.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`

- **Japan’s Kishida championed new capitalism but was undone by yen** | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | [URL](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen)  
  Reuters says Kishida achieved major wage gains, but the weak yen and high prices blunted results; that is mixed evidence that competent management did not fully overcome external constraints.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `5B.7`, `5B.10`, `6B.2`

- **Kishida will not run for reelection** | Reuters | 2024-08-14 | [URL](https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/japan-pm-kishida-wont-run-for-reelection-at-ldp-race-kyodo-reports-3570455)  
  Reuters framed his exit as driven by scandals and living-cost anger, which shows political pressure was shaping the governing environment even where the policy apparatus was professional.  
  QIDs: `6B.4`, `5B.5`, `5B.7`, `6B.2`

**Search gap**
- I found **strong direct evidence** for professionalized funding/management of children’s policy, disaster relief, healthcare/nursing-care subsidies, local grants, and budget setting through formal councils and expert input.
- I found **little direct evidence of patronage within social-service agencies themselves**. The main negative evidence is indirect: scandal pressure, coalition bargaining, and fragile macro conditions.
- I did **not** find a clear 2024 example of Kishida openly using social-service budgets to reward loyalists or bypass competent administrators.
